trajectory_summary: The call opens on a wrong-name stumble and spends its middle stretch fielding a customer who probes the rep's role and repeatedly tries to get the proposal sent directly to him rather than via appointment. The rep holds scope and holds the hard proposal rule, gets through the verify section, and ultimately locks a Saturday appointment — but a late scheduling-system delay draws a pointed, unresolved criticism from the customer that the rep never directly answers, closing the call on a sour note despite the booked time.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Saturday) and time (09:30) are agreed by the customer with an explicit 'Yes,' satisfying the booked threshold. No spouse or co-owner was identified (customer confirmed no one else is on the title), so co_owner_confirmed is null.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks what interested the customer in solar; the call moves from program explanation directly into address/verify questions without a dedicated interest question, so there is no stated customer motivation to reinforce later.

key_moments.stewart_read: The rep opens by calling the customer 'Glenn' — a wrong name — and the recovery at 00:13 ('is this Li Yoon... it is a home') is muddled rather than clean, meaning legitimacy is not cleanly established in the first 30 seconds as the schema requires.

key_moments.stewart_read: The customer asks a genuine closer-tier technical question about excess energy/net metering. The rep does not fabricate an answer and instead deploys the universal escape hatch, deferring cleanly to the specialist. This is schema-compliant scope discipline, not a failure to answer.

This is the third touch of the customer trying to get the proposal sent directly rather than delivered on the appointment call. The rep holds the hard rule (no cave, no promise to email) but answers with a bare 'No' and a redirect, never giving the canonical justification ('our proposals require full explanation otherwise they're confusing'). Per the deviation grading, this lands as held_line_with_improvisation rather than a clean scripted hold.
